sources.label: Researcher report schema and existing schema test
sources.summary: ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.superRefine contains four checks; check 3 rejects string blockers for design-validation scopes. Existing test coverage at plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.test.ts lines 415-451 explicitly expects that schema-time rejection.

sources.label: Submit-handler write boundary
sources.summary: executeSubmit parses first, loads the change, then performs the AC13 approved-contract-ID check. Its flatMap explicitly maps string blockers to an empty array, so strings do not crash the current AC13 check.

sources.label: Recovery writer
sources.summary: RecoverySubagentReport is a loose structural interface; saveRecoveredSubagentReport accepts it directly and does not parse through ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.

sources.label: Subagent report capability law
sources.summary: rq-subagentReports24.1 applies to a new report when adv_subagent_report_submit validates it; the body requires malformed input rejection before mutation while preserving readability of legacy persisted researcher reports.

sources.label: Zod refinement documentation
sources.summary: Zod documents that superRefine adds validation issues during parsing; moving a refinement out of the shared schema is therefore necessary to make historical parse paths tolerant.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Existing pattern: a shared Zod schema handles both persisted reads and new-submit parsing, while check 3 imposes a new-write policy on every parse (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L541-L604). Reference pattern for this repository: legacy normalization/read compatibility remains separate from strict submit ingestion (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L875-L881), and rq-subagentReports24.1 names adv_subagent_report_submit as the new-report enforcement boundary (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.adv/specs/subagent-reports/spec.json#L1181-L1193). Chosen relocation is architecturally correct and simpler than migration, coercion, or poisoned-history recovery. Deviation in design completeness is material: an existing test explicitly pins schema-time string rejection, contrary to the design's no-existing-test/no-change claim (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.test.ts#L415-L451). Spec-law implication: no spec delta is needed, but implementation cannot satisfy AC1/AC5 until that test is deliberately rewritten. C7's required error precedence remains testable, but its crash rationale is inaccurate because current flatMap already guards strings (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts#L761-L769).

blockers.finding: Design misses an existing test that explicitly expects ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.parse to reject a design-validation string blocker with /typed contract IDs/. Removing check 3 will fail that test, so the stated test plan and 'no changes expected' inventory cannot satisfy AC1/AC5 as written.
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Update the existing researcher judgement-consistency test: replace the schema-time string-rejection assertion with a successful legacy parse/preservation assertion, while retaining separate assertions for the other three superRefine invariants. Keep the new executeSubmit rejection test for AC3.

source.label: Existing schema-time rejection test
source.summary: Lines 428-430 call ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.parse with a design-validation string blocker and expect /typed contract IDs/, directly pinning check 3 at schema parse time.

blockers.finding: C7/design says bare strings would crash the existing AC13 flatMap, but current handler explicitly branches on typeof blocker === "string" and returns [], so no contract_ids dereference occurs. Ordering is still required to preserve AC3's specific string-blocker rejection before unknown-ID diagnostics, not to prevent a crash.
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Correct C7's design rationale to error-precedence/rejection-semantics preservation. Keep the proposed ordering test with a mixed string plus unknown-ID typed blocker and assert the stringBlockerIndices error wins; do not describe the current code as crash-prone.

source.label: Current AC13 flatMap string guard
source.summary: The existing unknown-ID flatMap maps string blockers to [] and accesses contract_ids only for typed blockers.

validation.notes: Core relocation passes architectural and spec-law review, but test inventory omission is implementation-blocking and C7 rationale contradicts source. Advisory fail only; no gate mutation is authorized by this report.

tradeoffs: Relocating policy to executeSubmit restores historical readability but duplicates a scoped semantic check outside the Zod schema, requiring handler-focused regression tests and a comment preventing schema-level reintroduction.
Keeping the blocker union read-tolerant preserves immutable historical text but means generic schema parsing alone no longer proves that a report was acceptable as a new submission.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep schema check and add describe() metadata
alternatives_considered.rationale: describe() adds metadata but does not stop superRefine from rejecting historical parses; it cannot satisfy AC1.

alternatives_considered.option: Return a typed warning instead of rejecting new string blockers
alternatives_considered.rationale: rq-subagentReports24.1 requires INVALID_REPORT rejection for new bare-string blockers.
The spec and C6 intentionally apply strict enforcement to every scope key starting with that prefix.
More complex, violates verbatim-history constraint C3, and is unnecessary when enforcement can live at the submit boundary.

alternatives_considered.option: Coerce legacy strings into typed blockers on read
alternatives_considered.rationale: Invents contract authority and remediation metadata, masks original history, and violates C3.
Wrong mechanism for schema-evolved readable data and substantially more complex than boundary relocation.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Revise the design/test inventory for the existing schema rejection test and correct C7's rationale; then proceed with the same tolerant-reader/strict-writer implementation and explicit mixed-blocker ordering test.

# Proposal: Make legacy design-validation blockers read-tolerant

## Objective

A change with legacy string-form design-validation blockers in historical reports must be readable, archivable, and completable through normal ADV tooling, without weakening the typed-blocker requirement for **new** submissions.

## Root cause (source-confirmed)

The typed-blocker requirement is enforced inside a Zod `superRefine` on `ResearcherSubagentReportSchema` (`plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts`, ~L580–591, "check-3"). That schema is reached on **every read** of `change.json`:

`ChangeSchema.subagent_reports` (`plugin/src/types/changes.ts:926`) → `ScopedSubagentReportSchema` (`subagent-reports.ts:803`) → `ChangeScopedSubagentReportSchema` discriminated union (L790) → `ResearcherSubagentReportSchema` (L541) → `.superRefine(...)` check-3.

The same schema is also the write validator: `adv_subagent_report_submit` parses incoming reports through `ScopedSubagentReportSchema.safeParse` (`plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts:179`). So a single enforcement point runs on both reads and writes — which is the defect. Records written before check-3 existed (plain-string design-validation blockers) now fail every read, wedging archive/gate/show for that change with `CONFLICT_INVENTORY_BLOCKED → Schema validation failed`.

Note: `ResearcherValidationSchema.blockers` is already `z.union([z.string(), ResearcherValidationBlockerSchema])` — the base schema was intentionally built to **parse** strings for backward-compat. Check-3 was bolted onto parse-time; it belongs at the write boundary.

Only check-3 breaks legacy data. The sibling superRefine checks (pass→confidence, fail→≥1 blocker, design-validation→applicable judgement) are legitimate parse invariants that historical valid reports already satisfy; they stay on the read path.

## Chosen direction: tolerant reader, strict writer

Move **only check-3** from the schema `superRefine` to the submit trust boundary. This is the structural fix (P33 / Postel): tolerate historical data on read, enforce current standards on write. No read-time coercion and no repair tool are needed — immutable history simply becomes readable, and archive proceeds on the normal path.

### Edit sites

1. **Remove check-3** from `ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.superRefine` (`subagent-reports.ts` ~L580–591). Keep the other three superRefine checks. `ChangeSchema.parse` now tolerates legacy string design-validation blockers.
2. **Re-add check-3 at the write boundary** in `plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts`, immediately after the successful `ScopedSubagentReportSchema.safeParse` (~L179–189): if `scope_key` starts with `researcher:design-validation` and any blocker is a `string`, reject with the existing "new design-validation blockers require typed contract IDs, in-scope remediation, and source evidence" message + the offending indices. New submissions remain strict.
3. **Recovery-writer tolerance:** confirm the `_recovery-writers.ts` report path does NOT re-impose check-3 (recovery is inherently for already-poisoned data). The single strict enforcement point is the normal `adv_subagent_report_submit` tool.

## Scope

- Relocate design-validation typed-blocker enforcement from parse-time to the submit tool.
- Ensure `adv_change_archive` conflict-inventory load, `adv_gate_complete`, `adv_change_show`, and `adv_task_show` succeed on a change with legacy string design-validation blockers.
- Confirm recovery-writer path stays tolerant.
- Regression tests (below).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A `change.json` whose historical `subagent_reports` contain string-form `researcher:design-validation` blockers passes `ChangeSchema.parse` on read (no superRefine failure); the other three researcher superRefine invariants still hold.
- **AC2:** `adv_change_archive` completes for such a change (conflict inventory loads; bundle written; status → archived; spec deltas applied) with no `poisoned_history` recovery and no direct `change.json` edits.
- **AC3:** A **new** `adv_subagent_report_submit` design-validation report containing a string blocker is still rejected with the typed-blocker guidance and offending indices (write-path strictness preserved).
- **AC4:** `adv_change_show` / `adv_task_show` / `adv_gate_complete` on such a change surface no schema error attributable to string design-validation blockers.
- **AC5:** Regression tests reproduce AC1–AC3 (read round-trip, archive-through, write rejection).

## Constraints / avoidances

- Do NOT weaken the typed-blocker requirement for **new** design-validation submissions.
- Do NOT weaken or remove the other three researcher `superRefine` checks.
- Do NOT silently rewrite or coerce historical blocker text at read time (read tolerance only; original strings preserved verbatim in state).
- Do NOT bundle with `fixPoisonedRecovery` or re-open #258 scope; separate contract, ships independently.
- Do NOT introduce a heuristic that could mask genuinely malformed **new** reports.

## Validation of the wedged case

After this ships, Vision change `fixPlaywrightSessionIsolation` (currently acceptance-done, un-archivable) archives on the normal path — its 5 `mcp-streamable-transport` deltas apply and it retires. Use it as the real-world AC2 fixture reference.

## Related

- #258 `fixRecoverySchemaDrift` (archived) — fixed schema-error surfacing + `recovery_audit` drift; sibling. Made the real error visible, did not add read-tolerance for legacy string blockers.
- `fixPoisonedRecovery` — sibling recovery work.
- Discovered completing Vision `fixPlaywrightSessionIsolation` (2026-07-20).
documents.problemStatement:
# Problem Statement

A change whose historical `subagent_reports` contain **string-form** design-validation blockers cannot be archived — or pass any workflow-touching ADV operation that schema-validates `change.json` — because the current schema **enforces typed blockers on every parse (read and write)**, with no migration or read-tolerance path for reports written before the typed-blocker schema landed.

## Reproduction (observed)

- Vision change `fixPlaywrightSessionIsolation` reached end-of-execution; its Temporal workflow was interrupted (poisoned record). Its design phase had 3 **failed** design-validation attempts (later superseded by a passing attempt 4). Those failed-attempt reports (`subagent_reports[1..3]`, scope `researcher:design-validation`) carry **plain-string** blockers — the format written at the time.
- `ResearcherValidationSchema.blockers` (`plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts`) is `z.union([z.string(), ResearcherValidationBlockerSchema])` — so strings **parse**. But the report `superRefine` (~L580) adds a custom issue for every string blocker on a `researcher:design-validation`-scoped report: *"new design-validation blockers require typed contract IDs, in-scope remediation, and source evidence."*
- Because this runs on **every** `ChangeSchema.parse` (reads included), the conflict-inventory load inside `adv_change_archive` fails: `CONFLICT_INVENTORY_BLOCKED → Active conflict authority unreachable: Schema validation failed for change "..."`.
- There is **no supported repair path**:
  - `adv_subagent_report_submit` dedups by report key (`changeId|scope_key|agent|attempt`) and **skips** same-key resubmits (`change-state.ts submitSubagentReport`, `_recovery-writers.ts`) — cannot overwrite the historical strings with typed versions.
  - `recoveryMode: "poisoned_history"` on archive requires workflow-execution poisoning tokens (`TMPRL1100` / `WorkflowNotFoundError` / `workflow execution already completed`) — this is **schema-evolved data**, not workflow poisoning, so it is rejected.
  - Archive loads the change through the workflow store, which re-derives the strings from immutable history — so editing the disk projection cannot reach it.

Net effect: the change is permanently un-archivable through ADV tooling, even though it is fully verified and shipped. In the observed case the code was merged to trunk out-of-band to unblock the machine, leaving the ADV change stuck at acceptance-done with its spec deltas unapplied.

## Why #258 does not cover this

`fixRecoverySchemaDrift` (#258) fixed schema-error **surfacing** (why the real message is now visible) and `recovery_audit` drift on dispositions. It did **not** address legacy **string design-validation blockers**, which have no migration or read-tolerance path. Related sibling: `fixPoisonedRecovery`.

# Executive Summary: makeLegacyDesignValidation

## Outcome

Legacy ADV changes whose historical `subagent_reports` contain string-form `researcher:design-validation` blockers are now fully readable, archivable, and completable through normal ADV tooling. The wedged Vision `fixPlaywrightSessionIsolation` change (acceptance-done, un-archivable since 2026-07-20) unblocks on the normal archive path.

## Value / why it matters

A schema-evolution defect made fully-verified, shipped changes permanently un-archivable: their spec deltas couldn't apply, and the ADV change couldn't retire. The code was already merged to trunk out-of-band to unblock the machine, but the ADV state was stuck at acceptance-done with no supported repair path. This change restores the archive path for any historical change in this shape — without weakening the typed-blocker requirement for new submissions.

## What was built

**Tolerant reader, strict writer** — relocated the "design-validation blockers must be typed" enforcement from `ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.superRefine` (parse-time, runs on every read) to the `adv_subagent_report_submit` handler `executeSubmit` (write-time only).

- **Schema** (`plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts`): removed check-3 from `ResearcherSubagentReportSchema.superRefine`. The three sibling checks (pass+low-confidence, fail+no-blockers, design-validation+not_applicable) stay. Added a relocation comment to prevent regressions.
- **Handler** (`plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts`): added a string-blocker check inside the existing design-validation `if`-block, BEFORE the AC13 unknown-contract-IDs `flatMap`. New bare-string blockers on new submissions are rejected with the same `INVALID_REPORT` + message + offending indices as before — only the location changed.
- **Recovery writer** (`plugin/src/tools/_recovery-writers.ts`): unchanged. Already used a loose structural interface; confirmed tolerant.

## Spec-conformance angle

This was a conformance fix, not a relaxation. Spec `rq-subagentReports24.1` already targets `adv_subagent_report_submit` as the enforcement boundary (`"when": "adv_subagent_report_submit validates the report"`). Spec body names the submit tool as the canonical preflight. The schema-time check-3 was an over-implementation beyond what the spec mandated.

## Verification

- **241 tests passed** across 9 affected test files (`bin/oc-test targeted`, 3.65s)
- **All 5 acceptance criteria green** (AC1 read tolerance, AC2 archive-through, AC3 write strictness, AC4 other read paths, AC5 regression tests)
- **All 7 constraints respected** (C1-C7)
- **All 6 avoidances respected** (DONT1-DONT6)
- **Independent reviewer verdict**: READY (141 focused tests + TypeScript check pass; contract implementation matches)
- **`pnpm run check` green** (schemas, typecheck, manifests, lint, format)

## Key design decisions

1. **Relocation over migration** — no data migration tool, no on-disk rewrite, no read-time coercion. Immutable history simply becomes readable.
2. **C7 ordering rationale corrected during design** — the original "crash prevention" rationale was inaccurate because the AC13 `flatMap` silently skips strings. Real motivation: **silent-acceptance prevention** — without the string check first, new bare-string blockers would slip through AC13 and persist via normal signaling.
3. **TDD red→green across task boundaries** — schema-check removal caused the existing test to fail; later test updates proved legacy tolerance. Production tasks captured red evidence via `adv_run_test`.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Real-world AC2 validation**: archive the Vision `fixPlaywrightSessionIsolation` change on its normal path after this release loads.
- **Runtime reload**: OpenCode does not hot-reload plugin modules. After merge/push, build and deploy from merged trunk, then restart OpenCode.
- **No other known risks**: no public API change, no spec delta, no recovery-path change, no new exported symbol.

## Release Readiness Summary

**Status: READY**

- Test/TDD: 241-test accepted sweep green; scanner rechecked 119 touched-file tests and found direct AC1/AC2/AC3/C7 boundary coverage.
- Residual slop/maintainability: no actionable findings; strict write guard remains structural and scope-bound.
- Documentation hygiene: inline relocation and ordering rationale accurate; one informational suggestion to make legacy read tolerance more explicit in generated spec prose, non-blocking.
- Cleanup: zero temp/debug/dead-import/orphan-test candidates.
- Production readiness: security, reliability, performance, maintainability, error semantics, and regression-risk checks READY.
- Deployment readiness: no env, migration, external-service, CI, or infrastructure changes. Standard post-merge build/deploy/restart required.
- Merge compatibility: clean dry-run merge against `origin/trunk`.
- Report-created follow-ups: 0 open required follow-ups; one prior test-command naming note already resolved.

## Approval Consequence Context

| Category | Status | Evidence / consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Delivered value | ready | Historical design-validation reports become readable and archivable while new malformed submissions remain rejected. |
| Enabling-only / dependency | warning | This release enables `reshapeTriagePortfolioBalance` validation and real-world archive recovery; those remain separate follow-on actions. |
| Ops readiness | ready | No ops runbook or production operation. Local plugin build/deploy/restart required after merge. |
| Migration / data impact | ready | No migration, no state rewrite, no coercion. Existing report strings remain verbatim. |
| Frontend / preview impact | not applicable | No frontend or browser surface changed. |
| Collision / release risk | ready | Clean merge simulation against `origin/trunk`; no blocker/high/medium harden findings. |
| Open follow-ups | warning | After release: restart OpenCode, verify legacy change readability, then resume blocked portfolio-balance validation. |
| Next action | ready | Sign off archive; direct-merge locally to trunk and push per operator instruction, then build/deploy merged trunk and restart OpenCode. |
